description: A spanned dataset, RECFM VBS: twenty-byte records in a file whose largest segment is sixteen bytes, so no segment carries more than twelve bytes of a record and neither record arrives in one piece. The first record is laid into the two segments a correct writer chooses, twelve bytes and then eight. The second is laid into three, eight and eight and four, which is a well-formed file that no correct writer would have produced -- a writer emits each record in as few segments as the largest allows -- so writing these records back gives a file whose bytes are not this one's while its values are the same. Both boundaries fall inside an item rather than between two, at twelve inside S-TEXT and at sixteen inside S-COUNT, so a consumer that decoded a segment instead of reassembling the record first fails on them.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "Four framings, and none of them is a RECFM", "Where framing is consumed, and where it is emitted" and "Lengths the file node does not carry"; docs/layout/SPEC.md, "Physical framing" and "lrecl and blksize describe the dataset, not the stream"; the segment descriptor word is DFSMS's, cited in docs/ir/SPEC.md's "Governing sources" and not restated there; docs/conformance/SPEC.md, "Why the writing direction is checked by reading, and not by comparing bytes"
